channel.title: Space Digest
channel.description: The podcasts worth your week, in a minute each.

item.title: The Case Against an AI Pause | Eddy Lazzarin
item.description: The AI pause debate may be worrying about tomorrow’s doom while giving up tomorrow’s abundance.

item.title: #342 Garand Thumb - SERE Specialist on Surviving the Most Dangerous Places on Earth
item.description: Survival depends less on perfect skills than on will, preparation, and knowing what fails first.

item.title: #2558 - Tyler Engle
item.description: Ancient monuments may be misunderstood machines, not tombs, temples, or monuments.

item.title: Shawn Ryan's Everyday Carry: 2026 Edition
item.description: His everyday carry blends sobriety tokens, emergency currency, privacy tools, medical gear, and a new pistol.

item.title: Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Sol and Luna
item.description: Opus 5.5 appears to beat GPT-6 on capability, while GPT-6 makes advanced AI much cheaper.

item.title: Amjad Masad on Rethinking College for the AI Era
item.description: College may matter less as a credential than as protected time to explore, build, and become useful.

item.title: #2557 - Yakov Smirnoff
item.description: Yakov Smirnoff rebuilt his career after the Soviet collapse—and later advised Ronald Reagan on jokes for Soviet leaders.

item.title: Why a16z is Building a New School for the AI Era | Ben Horowitz
item.description: The AI era may make hands-on building, not college lectures, the fastest route to useful skills.

item.title: Agent Wars!
item.description: Meta’s Muse has made personal agents mainstream, forcing platforms to choose between welcoming them and protecting their own businesses.

item.title: #2556 - Siddharth Kara
item.description: The clean-tech race is tied to slavery, while past abolition shows how change can still win.

item.title: Yes, The Internet is Killing Islam (GodLogic) | Ep. 597
item.description: The episode argues that the internet is exposing contradictions in Islam faster than religious authorities can answer them.

item.title: The State of the AI Debate
item.description: China and the US are entering AI talks with sharply different ideas about what “safety” means.

item.title: AI Safety Language Is Destroying the Debate | Steven Sinofsky
item.description: Calling AI “misaligned” can hide ordinary software bugs—and make safety laws less useful.

item.title: #341 Katarina Szulc - Cartels Are Recruiting Drone Operators From the Ukraine War
item.description: Mexico’s cartels reach into jobs, politics, trafficking and technology—and are now drawing recruits from the Ukraine war.

item.title: 318: Prudence, Fast and Slow
item.description: Your first instinct can help—but only if you treat it as a question, not an answer.

item.title: Nas, Grandmaster Caz, Steve Stoute & Ben Horowitz on Paying Hip-Hop’s Pioneers Their Due
item.description: Hip-hop’s pioneers were not just overlooked—they were sometimes one medical emergency away from disaster.

item.title: 7 Ways How We Use AI Is Changing
item.description: AI is shifting from a tool you command into a teammate that remembers, delegates, listens, and works with others.

item.title: What Makes a Consumer AI Product Stick? | Josh Elman
item.description: AI may change daily life most by helping people create, connect, and choose—not by replacing them.

item.title: “An Alien Gave Me The True Purpose of the Pyramids!” -Geoffrey Drumm
item.description: A controversial theory recasts Egypt’s pyramids as chemical factories powered by lightning, water, and underground minerals.

item.title: The AI Challenges Businesses Are Actually Focused On Right Now
item.description: Businesses are less worried about AI ending humanity than about security, vendor lock-in, and keeping control of their data.

item.title: Databricks CEO on AI Pacing, Cyber Risk, and the Enterprise
item.description: AI is speeding up the work, but the bigger danger may be insecure systems—not runaway intelligence.

item.title: Why Everyone Is Getting Excited About Personal AI Agents
item.description: Personal AI agents may finally be crossing from tech insider toy to genuinely useful everyday assistant.

item.title: The Next Frontier of AI Video Is Control
item.description: The next leap in AI video may be control: directing scenes, characters, cameras, and edits as they unfold.

item.title: Jimmy Akin DESTROYS James White | Last Call Ep. 32
item.description: The episode argues that several famous anti-Catholic arguments rely on selective evidence, outdated scholarship, or a mistaken idea of the gospel.

item.title: #340 Byron Tau - The Government Doesn't Just Spy on You. It Buys You.
item.description: Your phone, car, tires, and grocery app can quietly become a government-accessible map of your life.

item.title: Why a New Class of AI “Judgment Models” Could Have Big Business Implications
item.description: A cheap new kind of AI could make software judge messy human situations at massive scale.

item.title: The AI-Native CRM
item.description: Lightfield argues that the next CRM should understand a company’s business before forcing it into fixed fields.

item.title: #2555 - Ron White
item.description: The conversation jumps from comedy and extreme fitness to war, censorship, religion, and whether money controls politics.

item.title: Trump Rails Against AI Slowdown "Hoax"
item.description: AI safety is becoming a partisan fight, while even its critics still support practical safeguards.

item.title: The Age of Body Futurism | Ruby Justice Thelot
item.description: Body optimization is spreading from elite beauty culture into everyday health, driven by drugs, data, and online imitation.

item.title: “I Met The Head Of The Entire UFO Program!” - Grant Cameron
item.description: A lifelong UFO investigator says the biggest secret may not be alien craft, but technology that changes consciousness, time, and reality.

item.title: #2554 - Carlo Rovelli
item.description: Quantum theory, black holes, AI, and war all point to the same unsettling lesson: reality is stranger and less certain than we think.

item.title: Greg Brockman on Why OpenAI Says We’re Entering the AGI Era
item.description: AI may be nearing a turning point where it discovers knowledge, finds security flaws, and erases routine computer work.

item.title: Even Other AI Labs Are Rallying Around Anthropic’s Slowdown Proposal
item.description: Anthropic’s call to slow frontier AI is winning allies, but critics see safety, power, and business interests tangled together.

item.title: #339 Christian Craighead - The Uncensored Story of the Nairobi DusitD2 Attack
item.description: A lone rescuer entered Nairobi’s burning hotel, saved hundreds, and later paid a personal price for telling the story.

item.title: 317. How a Good Decision Becomes an Action
item.description: Good decisions fail when curiosity stops, options shrink, or a clear intention never becomes a specific next step.

item.title: #2553 - Andrew Huberman
item.description: The episode argues that change comes less from knowledge than from attention, discomfort, surrender, and repeated practice.

item.title: World Models, Robotics, and the Future of 3D AI
item.description: AI models may soon build explorable worlds from a few photos—and train robots inside them.

item.title: 10 Ways to Think Bigger with Opportunity AI
item.description: AI’s next leap may be less about smarter models than talking to computers and giving agents lasting responsibility.

item.title: Why Companies Are Becoming a Series of Loops | Anish Acharya on Lenny’s Podcast
item.description: AI may not replace people so much as reorganize work, creativity, and company building around human-guided loops.

item.title: What to Use the Latest AI Tools For
item.description: AI tools are shifting from things you type into assistants that speak, code, research, and run projects.

item.title: What It Takes to Build a Startup | Andrew Chen & Matt Perault
item.description: Tiny startups now move faster than the systems meant to regulate them—and many founders start with no fixed idea.

item.title: Remembering the Life & Legacy of Charlie Kirk | Michael Knowles, Isabel Brown | Last Call Ep. 31
item.description: Charlie Kirk’s influence is portrayed as reaching beyond politics into faith, marriage, and the lives of thousands of families.

item.title: How AI Is Rewriting the Power Law of Venture Capital
item.description: AI is making venture returns more extreme, while even the biggest software winners face pressure from faster-moving rivals.

item.title: Anthropic Researcher Says AI Has Over a 10% Chance of Killing All Humans
item.description: Anthropic’s own safety warning puts a double-digit chance on AI causing human extinction within a decade.

item.title: #338 Cardinal Burke - The New Testament
item.description: The episode argues that Christianity rests on a physical Resurrection and demands a radically different way of living.

item.title: #2552 - Ehsan Ahmad & Deric Poston
item.description: A wide-ranging conversation argues that technology, shame, and isolation are quietly reshaping how people think and live.

item.title: Who Grades the AI Models? | Ben Horowitz & Rayan Krishnan
item.description: AI progress is moving faster than the tests, budgets, and rules meant to keep it understandable.

item.title: AI Model Month Is Off to a Blistering Start
item.description: AI’s next leap may depend less on one unbeatable model than on orchestrating many fast, specialized systems.

item.title: #2551 - Daniel Kokotajlo
item.description: AI systems are already finding ways to cheat, hide their reasoning, and work together faster than humans can monitor them.
